title: Domain VI: Contract Development & Administration - Contract Development & Administration - Ordering & Receiving
subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: Which mechanism is typically used to formally initiate a specific transaction, obligate funds, and instruct a vendor to deliver goods against an established master term contract?
options: A Purchase Requisition
An Invoice
A Purchase Order
A Packing Slip
questions.explain: A Purchase Order (PO) is the primary ordering document used to authorize a vendor to deliver specific goods or services under the terms of a master contract, effectively encumbering funds.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: A shipping term states 'FOB Destination'. Who bears the risk of loss or damage while the goods are in transit?
options: The Buyer (Receiving Agency)
The Freight Carrier
The Seller (Vendor)
Both the Buyer and Seller equally
questions.explain: Under 'FOB Destination' terms, the seller holds the title and bears the risk of loss until the goods are physically delivered to and accepted at the buyer's specified destination.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: If goods are shipped 'FOB Origin', at what exact point does the title and risk of loss transfer to the purchasing agency?
options: When the goods are delivered to the agency's loading dock.
When the goods are loaded onto the carrier at the seller's facility.
When the agency formally issues payment.
When the agency completes a functional inspection of the goods.
questions.explain: In 'FOB Origin', title and risk of loss transfer to the buyer the moment the goods are placed in the possession of the transport carrier at the seller's shipping dock.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: Upon receiving a shipment of laptops, the receiving clerk notices the boxes are heavily crushed. This type of easily observable defect is legally categorized as a:
options: Latent Defect
Constructive Defect
Patent Defect
Material Breach
questions.explain: A patent defect is an obvious flaw or damage that can be easily discovered through an ordinary, visual inspection of the goods upon receipt.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: Three months after accepting and using a batch of steel pipes, the agency discovers a hidden internal metallurgical flaw that causes the pipes to burst. Because this flaw could not have been discovered during routine receiving inspection, it is classified as a:
options: Patent Defect
Latent Defect
Force Majeure Event
Mutual Mistake
questions.explain: A latent defect is a hidden flaw that exists at the time of acceptance but cannot be discovered through a reasonable and customary inspection process.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: Under the Uniform Commercial Code (UCC), what fundamental right does the buyer possess before becoming legally obligated to pay for delivered goods?
options: The right to return the goods within 90 days for any reason.
The right to a reasonable opportunity to inspect the goods.
The right to immediately terminate the contract if the delivery is one day late.
The right to require the seller to assemble the goods at no cost.
questions.explain: The UCC grants buyers the right to a reasonable opportunity to inspect goods after delivery to ensure they conform to contract specifications before acceptance and payment.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: An agency receives a delivery of furniture that does not match the contractual specifications. What is the immediate legal right of the agency regarding the non-conforming goods?
options: The agency must accept the goods and demand a 50% discount.
The agency can reject the non-conforming goods entirely, accept them all, or accept any commercial unit and reject the rest.
The agency must immediately file a lawsuit against the vendor.
The agency must accept the goods but cancel all future orders.
questions.explain: According to the UCC's Perfect Tender Rule (or commercial variations thereof), if goods fail to conform to the contract, the buyer may reject the whole, accept the whole, or accept any conforming commercial units and reject the rest.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: What does 'Constructive Acceptance' mean in the context of receiving goods?
options: The goods were explicitly accepted in writing by the agency's inspector.
The agency failed to reject the goods within a reasonable time after delivery, thereby legally accepting them by default.
The goods were accepted despite known patent defects.
The goods were accepted by the end-user rather than the central receiving department.
questions.explain: Constructive acceptance occurs when the buyer retains the goods without giving notice of rejection to the seller within a reasonable timeframe, legally implying that the goods are accepted.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: Accounts payable processes an invoice for payment using the 'Three-Way Match' system. Which three documents are being matched?
options: Purchase Order, Packing Slip, and Requisition
Purchase Order, Receiving Report, and Vendor Invoice
Solicitation, Contract, and Vendor Invoice
Receiving Report, Vendor Invoice, and Check
questions.explain: A three-way match verifies that the Purchase Order, the Receiving Report (confirming goods were received), and the Vendor's Invoice all match before payment is issued.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: Which transportation document serves as a receipt issued by a carrier to the shipper, detailing the type, quantity, and destination of the goods being carried?
options: Purchase Order
Packing Slip
Bill of Lading
Receiving Report
questions.explain: A Bill of Lading is a legally binding document issued by a carrier to a shipper that serves as a receipt for freight services, a contract of carriage, and a document of title.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: A vendor delivers an over-shipment (delivers 120 items when the PO requested 100). If the agency decides to keep the extra 20 items, what must occur?
options: The agency pays nothing for the extra items.
The vendor is penalized with liquidated damages.
The contract or PO must be modified to accept the overage, and the agency must pay for the additional items.
The agency must return all 120 items and require exactly 100 to be re-shipped.
questions.explain: If a buyer elects to retain over-shipped quantities, they must pay for them at the contract rate, which typically requires a modification to the purchase order to reflect the increased quantity.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: When receiving goods, what is the primary purpose of the packing slip enclosed in the shipment?
options: To serve as the final invoice for payment processing.
To provide an itemized list of the items actually contained in that specific shipment package.
To transfer the legal title of the goods.
To document the transportation carrier's routing details.
questions.explain: A packing slip is provided by the shipper to list the exact contents of the physical package, enabling the receiving clerk to verify that everything shipped has arrived.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: If a procurement contract utilizes a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA), how are actual orders placed against it?
options: By issuing individual delivery orders or calls as needs arise during the term.
By paying the entire estimated contract value upfront.
By re-bidding each individual order among the pre-qualified vendors.
By verbal request without any written documentation.
questions.explain: A BPA sets up charge accounts with qualified sources. Actual purchases are made by placing individual 'calls' or delivery orders against the BPA when specific items or services are needed.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: A vendor delivers specialized software. The agency runs an agreed-upon series of tests to ensure it performs according to the statement of work before accepting it. This process is called:
options: Latent Defect Discovery
User Acceptance Testing (UAT)
Constructive Acceptance
Random Sampling Inspection
questions.explain: User Acceptance Testing (UAT) is the final phase of testing where the end-users verify that the delivered system functions correctly according to contractual requirements before formal acceptance.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: Even after formal acceptance, an agency retains the right to revoke acceptance and require the vendor to fix the problem under which of the following circumstances?
options: The agency finds a lower price from another vendor.
A patent defect is discovered one year later.
A latent defect is discovered that substantially impairs the value of the goods.
The end-user simply decides they do not like the color.
questions.explain: Revocation of acceptance is generally legally permissible when a defect that substantially impairs the value of the goods could not have been discovered during normal receiving inspection (latent defect).
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: If a carrier delays unloading a delivery truck at an agency's receiving dock beyond the allotted time, the carrier may assess a penalty charge to the agency known as:
options: Demurrage
Liquidated Damages
Retainage
Freight Fencing
questions.explain: Demurrage is a charge assessed by carriers for holding equipment (like trucks or shipping containers) beyond the permitted free time allocated for loading or unloading.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: Which of the following describes a situation where a buyer returns rejected goods to the seller, and the seller charges a fee to place the items back into their inventory?
options: Demurrage Charge
Restocking Fee
Indemnification Cost
Cancellation Penalty
questions.explain: A restocking fee is an administrative charge assessed by a vendor when a buyer returns items, compensating the vendor for the cost of processing and returning the items to stock.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: To effectively process a partial delivery under a purchase order, what administrative action is vital?
options: Canceling the original purchase order completely.
Documenting exactly what was received so a partial payment can be authorized while leaving the balance open.
Withholding all payment until the entire order is completely fulfilled.
Initiating a cure notice immediately for the undelivered portion.
questions.explain: For partial deliveries, receiving reports must accurately reflect only the quantities delivered so that AP can issue partial payments, keeping the PO open for backordered items.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: In expedited purchasing, when a buyer calls a supplier to urge them to accelerate a delayed shipment, this contract administration activity is referred to as:
options: Expediting
Mitigating
Ratifying
Terminating
questions.explain: Expediting is the process of attempting to speed up the delivery of goods or completion of services that are delayed or urgently needed.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: An agency receives goods shipped FOB Destination that arrive visibly damaged. What is the appropriate initial action by the receiving clerk?
options: Accept the goods and fix the damage using agency funds.
Note the damage on the Bill of Lading, refuse the damaged portion, and notify the vendor.
Sue the freight carrier directly for breach of contract.
Pay the invoice immediately to avoid late fees.
questions.explain: Because FOB Destination places the risk of loss on the seller, the agency should note the damage on the delivery receipt/bill of lading, refuse the damaged items, and immediately contact the seller for replacement.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration
